app_rules.float.help:
Floating takes this app's matching windows out of tiling: each keeps its last position and size and stays above the tiled windows, instead of snapping into one Space's grid.

This is per-app floating — not the **Floating** layout mode, which floats every window in a Space.

general.advanced.backup.error.empty: That backup is empty — there's nothing in it to restore.
general.advanced.backup.error.lua_owned: This Mac's settings come from your init.lua, so a backup's settings can't be applied here. Switch to the visual editor first, or restore onto a Mac that uses it.
general.advanced.backup.error.newer: That backup was made by a newer version of KiwiDesk. Update KiwiDesk, then try again.
general.advanced.backup.error.not_a_back: That file isn't a KiwiDesk backup.
general.advanced.backup.error.unreadable: That file couldn't be opened. It may have been moved, renamed, or deleted.
KiwiDesk can't read this Mac's settings file, so a backup would leave your settings out. Fix or reset the configuration first.
general.advanced.backup.error.write_fail: KiwiDesk couldn't write “%1$@”. Try somewhere else, like your Desktop.
general.advanced.backup.export.caption: Saves your settings, profiles, and color palettes to a file you choose. Doesn't include init.lua.
general.advanced.backup.export.help: A one-time snapshot, saved to a file you choose. KiwiDesk doesn't keep backups on its own — export again whenever you want an up-to-date copy.
general.advanced.backup.restore.caption: Replaces your settings, profiles, and color palettes with what's in a backup file. Doesn't touch init.lua.
This replaces your settings, every profile, and your color palettes with what's in the backup file — and discards any changes you haven't saved yet. The files being replaced go to the Trash. init.lua is never touched.
general.advanced.backup.restore.help: Replaces everything currently saved — your settings, every profile, and your color palettes — with what's in the chosen file. The versions being replaced go to the Trash. init.lua is never touched.
general.advanced.discard_arrangement.cap: Clears the arrangement KiwiDesk remembered from your last session or wake, without changing any settings.
general.advanced.discard_arrangement.hel: If windows come back in the wrong Spaces or positions after a restart or wake, a stale saved arrangement is the usual cause. Discarding it makes the next restore start clean — settings and profiles are untouched.
general.advanced.edit_lua.caption: Opens the integrated Lua editor for custom scripting beyond the visual controls.
general.advanced.reset_all.caption: Deletes your profiles, Spaces, layouts, and keybindings, then starts fresh with KiwiDesk's defaults. Doesn't touch init.lua or your color palettes.
general.advanced.reset_all.confirm.messa: This deletes every saved profile, your Spaces, layouts, and keybindings, and forgets any window arrangement KiwiDesk remembered — then starts over with its starter defaults, the same state as a first launch. Your init.lua and color palettes are kept. The old files go to the Trash.
general.advanced.reset_all.confirm.title: Reset all KiwiDesk settings?
general.advanced.reset_all.help: The last resort when KiwiDesk keeps misbehaving and discarding the saved arrangement didn't help: everything returns to a known-good default, the same state as a first launch.
general.advanced.restart_on_crash.needs_: Needs “%1$@”, because the two are one setting to macOS.

key_recorder.help_press: A shortcut is one key plus any of ⌃ Control, ⌥ Option, ⇧ Shift, and ⌘ Command — it locks in the moment you press the key. Add a layer to give one key a second meaning.
key_recorder.live_applied: Active now — Save to keep it

key_recorder.live_denied: Recorded — the system didn't grant it
key_recorder.live_profile_shadowed: Recorded — the active profile overrides it

keybinding.conflict.unrecognized: Shortcut for "%1$@" isn't a recognized shortcut.
keybinding.toggle_display_sticky.help: Keeps this window visible on every Space of the monitor it lives on. Moving it to a Space on another monitor re-homes it there. Turn a sticky window fully global with Toggle sticky.
keybinding.toggle_sticky.help: Keeps this window visible on every Space. A tiled sticky window can be rearranged only on its home Space — elsewhere, its position follows automatically. A floating sticky window isn't affected — it moves freely everywhere.
layout.bsp.blurb: Every new window splits the one it lands on, so the screen fills without ever overlapping.
layout.bsp.name: BSP
layout.floating.name: Floating
layout.grid.blurb: Equal cells. A dynamic grid rebalances as windows come and go; a rigid one keeps its shape.
layout.grid.name: Grid
layout.monocle.blurb: Every window fills the screen, one at a time, and focus cycles through them.
layout.monocle.name: Monocle
layout.schematic.bsp.ax: BSP preview: width ratio %1$d percent, height ratio %2$d percent; the plus tile is where the next window lands.
layout.schematic.bsp.caption_alternating: Splits alternate horizontal then vertical; the + tile is where the next window opens.
layout.schematic.bsp.caption_longest: Each split cuts the longer side; the + tile is where the next window opens.
layout.schematic.floating.ax: Floating preview: windows overlap where the user left them.
layout.schematic.floating.caption: Windows stay where you put them, and overlap. Your shortcuts still work.
layout.schematic.grid.caption_rigid: A fixed %1$d × %2$d grid; each window shrinks to a cell, extras stack in the last.
layout.schematic.grid.caption_rigid_auto: A fixed grid sized to your screen (about %1$d × %2$d); each window shrinks to a cell.
layout.schematic.grid.order_capped: %1$@ It balances up to %2$d × %3$d, then the surplus stacks in the last cell.
layout.schematic.grid.order_columns: New windows fill across a row, then wrap down.
layout.schematic.grid.order_rows: New windows fill down a column, then wrap across.
layout.schematic.monocle.ax: Monocle preview: one window fills the screen; focus cycles through the others.
layout.schematic.monocle.ax_park: Monocle preview: one window fills the screen; the others park in a corner, and focus switches instantly.
layout.schematic.monocle.caption_h: All windows fill the screen; new ones come to the front, and focus cycles left/right.
layout.schematic.monocle.caption_park_h: The focused window fills the screen and the rest park in a corner; new ones come to the front, and focus snaps left/right.
layout.schematic.monocle.caption_park_v: The focused window fills the screen and the rest park in a corner; new ones come to the front, and focus snaps up/down.
layout.schematic.monocle.caption_v: All windows fill the screen; new ones come to the front, and focus cycles up/down.
layout.schematic.scrolling.ax_anchored: Scrolling preview: a row of windows moving through the screen frame; the focused window rests at the anchor and the row scrolls past it.
layout.schematic.scrolling.ax_follow: Scrolling preview: a row of windows moving through the screen frame; %1$@ pans the row the minimum needed to reveal the focused window, keeping the side you came from in view.
layout.schematic.scrolling.caption_ancho: The focused window rests at the anchor and the row scrolls past it. %1$@
layout.schematic.scrolling.caption_follo: %1$@ pins the focused window nowhere: the row pans the minimum needed to reveal it, so the side you came from stays in view. %2$@
layout.schematic.scrolling.insertion: The + marks where the next window opens.
layout.schematic.stack.ax: Stack preview: %1$d master windows, master ratio %2$d percent; the plus tile is where the next window lands.
layout.schematic.stack.caption_all: Master zone and stack zone; when the stack fills, the whole zone piles so only the top edges show.
layout.schematic.stack.caption_overflow: Master zone and stack zone; when the stack fills, the surplus piles up.
layout.schematic.track.ax: Track preview: tracks along one axis, the far one piling overflow; the plus is the next window.
layout.schematic.track.ax_plain: Track preview: tracks along one axis; the plus is the next window.
layout.schematic.track.caption_focused: New windows join the focused track until it is full, then open one beside it; the far track piles the overflow.
layout.schematic.track.caption_focused_p: New windows join the focused track until it is full, then open one beside it.
layout.schematic.track.caption_own: New windows open their own track; the far track piles the overflow.
layout.schematic.track.caption_own_plain: New windows open their own track.
layout.scrolling.blurb: One endless row of fixed-width windows; the screen pans along it to the focused one.
layout.scrolling.name: Scrolling
layout.stack.blurb: One or more master windows beside a stack of the rest, which piles up once it fills.
layout.stack.name: Stack
layout.track.blurb: A more advanced layout: several windows can share one track, with a track limit and per-track resize.
layout.track.name: Track
layout_defaults.min_window_size_caption: Windows never tile smaller than this — it also caps auto-sized grids and track limits.
layout_defaults.spaces_using.none: No Space uses this layout yet — set one to it in %1$@.
layout_defaults.spaces_using.overridden_: %1$d of them override these values — edit them in %2$@.
1 of them overrides these values — edit it in %1$@.
layout_params.master_orientation.help: How the master zone lines up its windows when the master count is more than one: stacked top to bottom, or side by side.
layout_params.master_orientation.one_mas: %1$@ only changes anything with more than one master window.
layout_params.overflow.stack.help:
**%1$@** — Keeps as many windows fully tiled as fit, then cascades only the extra ones at the bottom.
**%2$@** — Cascades the whole stack, showing a sliver of every window.
layout_params.overflow.track.help:
How the far-edge **overflow track** — which collects the tracks that don't fit side by side — packs its windows.
**%1$@** (the default) — piles every window from the top.
**%2$@** — tiles what fits, piles the rest.
An ordinary track that holds more windows than fit always overflows this second way; only the far-edge track is configurable.
layout_params.split_ratio_h.help: How much of a side-by-side split's width goes to the earlier window; the later window gets the rest. Applies to every left/right split.
layout_params.split_ratio_v.help: How much of a stacked split's height goes to the earlier window; the later window gets the rest. Applies to every top/bottom split.
layout_params.split_strategy.help:
**%1$@** — Cuts whichever side of the region is longer, keeping new windows close to square.
**%2$@** — Alternates left/right and top/bottom cuts as the layout gets deeper, regardless of shape.
layout_params.stack_position.help: Which side of the screen the stack zone takes; the master zone gets the other side. The stack lines up to fit its strip: a left or right stack runs top to bottom, a top or bottom stack side by side.
layout_params.wrap_focus.help: When on, moving focus past the last window wraps around to the first, and past the first back to the last, instead of stopping at the end.

monocle.hide_style.help:
**%1$@** — Hidden windows stay behind the focused one, at full size.
**%2$@** — Hidden windows park in a corner instead, and focus changes instantly. Choose this when the windows behind show — through a transparent window, or around one that can't fill the whole screen. A thin edge of each parked window stays visible in the corner.

native_spaces.empty: No native macOS Desktops detected. Add Desktops in Mission Control to bind profiles.
native_spaces.help: Only Desktops on your main screen can be bound, because macOS's "Displays have separate Spaces" gives every screen its own Desktops by default. Turn it off, in System Settings ▸ Desktop & Dock, and every Desktop is shared across your screens instead — all of them bindable, at the cost of each screen's own menu bar, its own Dock, and fullscreen windows that no longer blank the others.
native_spaces.intro: These are your Mac's own Desktops, from Mission Control — not KiwiDesk's Spaces. Pick a profile to load automatically when a Desktop activates on your main screen (the one with the menu bar).

scroll_grid.app_bar_xref_state: The scrolling App Bar (currently %1$@) is configured in %2$@.
scroll_grid.auto_size.dimensions_inert: An auto-sized grid takes its columns and rows from the screen.
scroll_grid.auto_size.gates: %1$@ is on, so the screen decides the columns and rows.
scroll_grid.auto_size.xref: %1$@ is on, so the screen decides the columns and rows — change it in %2$@.
scroll_grid.auto_size_caption: Fits as many columns and rows as the screen allows, using the minimum window size above.
scroll_grid.fill_empty_cells.rigid_only: A rigid grid keeps every cell, so an empty cell stays empty rather than being filled.
scroll_grid.scroll_speed.animation_off: Focus shifts jump straight to the slot while %1$@ is off.

shortcuts.advanced.caption: Bind any Lua to a hotkey. This is the power-user escape hatch — the groups above cover the built-in actions.
shortcuts.advanced.title: Lua bindings
shortcuts.app_behavior.help:
**%1$@** brings the app's existing window to the current Space, or launches it if the app isn't running. Pressing again while that window is focused cycles through the app's other windows. If the app has nothing on screen, pressing the shortcut restores its most recently minimized window; otherwise minimized windows stay in the Dock.

**%2$@** always launches a fresh instance, even when the app is already open.
shortcuts.apps.empty: No app has a key of its own yet. Add one and its key brings that app's window to the Space you're on, or launches the app if it isn't running.
shortcuts.base_layer_protected: Base layers can't be removed here
shortcuts.import.help: Reads the shortcuts active in init.lua and adds them here, matching each combo. Known actions sort into the groups below; anything else lands in “%1$@”. Review, then Save.
shortcuts.inactive.caption: These shortcuts target Spaces that are not in the current Space list. They still work — pressing one recreates its Space — and they keep their key combo. Rebind or remove them here; they become active again when their Space returns.
shortcuts.layers.caption: Layers are alternate shortcut sets — only the active layer's shortcuts fire. Bind a key below to switch between them. “default” is the standard layer and is always the active one after the app starts.
shortcuts.move_to_track.caption: Only relevant if you're using the track layout.
shortcuts.override.caption: Dimmed rows are inherited from the base shortcuts and stay in sync with them. Edit a row to override it for this profile only; matching the base again makes it inherited again. Removing an inherited row only resets it — to disable a combo in this profile, rebind it to a no-op action instead.
shortcuts.override.staged: Editing “%1$@” — shortcuts take effect the next time this profile is active.
shortcuts.override.staged_loaded: Editing “%1$@” — shortcuts re-apply as soon as you save.
shortcuts.override.title: Profile shortcuts
shortcuts.panel.dismiss_hint: Esc or click away to close
shortcuts.panel.inactive.caption: These target Spaces that are not in the current Space list. They still work — pressing one recreates its Space — and they come back when their Space returns.
shortcuts.panel.unavailable: Shortcuts are managed by your init.lua.
shortcuts.row.inherited.axhint: Inherited from the base shortcuts. Set a key here to override it.
shortcuts.size_float.feedback: Alert sound when resize can't apply
shortcuts.size_float.layouts_caption: Grow/Shrink only applies in the bsp, stack, scrolling, and track layouts; it is a no-op in monocle, grid, and floating. Width and height resize independently; scrolling resizes its slot along the scroll axis for both, and in track one axis resizes the window's track, the other its share within it.
space_bar.active_indicator.label: Active indicator
space_bar.alignment.label: Alignment
space_bar.alignment.label.help: Where the Space items — and the front-app segment, when shown — sit along the bar. “%1$@” and “%2$@” follow the edge, so on a left bar the start of the bar is its top.
space_bar.background_fit.boxed_only: “%1$@” draws a box per item, not a shared plate, so there is nothing to size.
space_bar.background_fit.label: Background size
space_bar.background_style.label: Background style
space_bar.color.active_space.help: Tints the active Space's identifier and its app glyphs.
space_bar.color.focused_item.help: Tints the focused window — its glyph in the active Space and the front-app segment. Glyph tint needs “%2$@” set to “%1$@”.
space_bar.color.group_badge.help: Count and overflow badges on the active Space; inactive Spaces mute them from the item color. Grouping is always on.
space_bar.colors.title: Space Bar colors
space_bar.disabled.help: Turn on %1$@ to edit these settings.
space_bar.edge.label: Position
space_bar.edge.label.help: Which screen edge the Space Bar occupies. Sharing an edge with the App Bar is fine — the two stack.
space_bar.enabled.help: One bar per display listing that display's Spaces — click a Space to switch to it. The bar reserves its edge in every layout.
space_bar.glyph_cap.help: How many app glyphs a Space shows before the rest collapse into a +n badge. Adjacent windows of the same app count as one glyph.
space_bar.glyph_cap.summary: Up to %1$d app groups per Space; more collapse into a +n badge.
space_bar.hide_empty.help: Spaces with no windows are hidden from the bar, except the Space you're currently on. Use a shortcut to jump to a hidden Space.
space_bar.icon_source.help: How app glyphs are drawn. “%1$@” shows a monochrome symbol colored by the bar's item colors, set in %2$@; apps without a symbol keep their app icon.
space_bar.icon_source.label: App symbol style
space_bar.show_front_app.help: Adds a trailing segment with the focused window of the Space each display currently shows. Icon-only on vertical bars.
space_bar.spring_delay.help: Drag a window onto a Space and hold this long for the view to spring to that Space, so you can drop the window into its layout. A quicker drop moves the window there without switching.
space_bar.title_cap.help: How many characters of the focused window's title the front segment shows before it is shortened.
space_override.caption: Unchecked settings inherit %1$@ defaults.
space_override.dormant.summary_many: Saved for %1$d other layouts — they apply if you switch this Space back.
space_override.dormant.summary_one: Saved for 1 other layout — it applies if you switch this Space back.
space_override.reset_active.none: There are no overrides to reset.
space_override.reset_all_confirm.message: This clears every layout's saved overrides for this Space, not just the current one. This can't be undone.
space_override.reset_all_confirm.title: Reset all layout overrides?
space_override.slot_size.help: Sets each scrolling window's size along the scroll direction — the column width when the orientation is %1$@, the row height when it is %2$@. As a unit, %3$@ scales with that width or height (95%% out of the box) and %4$@ fixes an exact size.
space_override.title: %1$@ — %2$@ overrides
spaces.caption: Each Space has its own layout. Add Spaces here; they appear in the shortcut and app-rule lists too. Drag rows to reorder.
spaces.delete_confirm.message: This Space has customized settings — its layout overrides, monitor pin, and any “%1$@” or “%2$@” role are removed too. You can add the Space back, but not its settings.
spaces.delete_confirm.title: Delete this Space?
spaces.empty: No Spaces yet — add one below. Until you do, every window tiles in a single default Space.
spaces.fallback_badge.help: Windows from a removed Space land here when you switch profiles.
spaces.fallback_caption: When you switch profiles, windows from a Space the new profile doesn't have land in its fallback Space (the first Space when none is chosen).
spaces.overrides.saved.help: Saved for other layouts — switch this Space to a tiling layout to use them.
spaces.pin_offline_badge.help: Pinned to a display that isn't attached, so this Space opens on the main display for now.

spaces.preview.title: This Space's layout
spaces.title: Spaces
sticky.caption: Sticky windows stay visible on every Space (%1$@, in %2$@).
sticky.display.pill: Can only be moved to a different display
sticky.everywhere.pill: Sticky windows can't be moved to another Space
sticky.home.pill: Can only be moved in its home Space %1$@
sticky.mark.help: A sticky window can look identical to a normal one, so KiwiDesk draws a small mark in its top-right corner. The mark is also how a refused move explains itself, whether you dragged the window or used a shortcut, so turning the mark off silences those messages too. The Space Bar shows its own sticky badge either way; hide the bar as well and no sticky signal is left.
sticky.pile.pill: Sticky windows can't be moved to the pile
sticky.title: Sticky windows
track.auto_tracks.gates: %1$@ is on, so the screen decides how many tracks open.
track.auto_tracks.limit_inert: The track limit follows the screen while %1$@ is on.
track.auto_tracks.xref: %1$@ is on, so the screen decides how many tracks open — change it in %2$@.
track.auto_tracks_caption: Fits as many tracks as the screen allows, using the minimum window size above — opening and collapsing them as windows come and go.
track.new_window_position.help: With “%1$@”, where the new track lands among the tracks; with “%2$@”, where the window lands inside that track: %3$@, %4$@, or right before or after the focused window.
